facts.claim: Australian citizens who want to marry in Italy need a Nulla Osta (an official statement that there is no impediment to the marriage), which must be presented to the Italian town council (Comune) where the wedding takes place, before the ceremony.
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia Sydney (esteri.it)
facts.use_note: H2 3. Explain Nulla Osta on first use. Close the section with: your Wedded Advisor confirms the current process for your passports.

facts.claim: To obtain the Nulla Osta, each Australian partner first signs an Atto Notorio, a sworn declaration of no impediment made with four witnesses who must not be related to the couple. It can be done in Australia at the Italian Consulate General or in Italy at a court (Tribunale).
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia Sydney (esteri.it)
facts.use_note: H2 3. Conflict on witness numbers: the Sydney consulate says four witnesses for an Atto Notorio made at the consulate; the Australian Embassy Rome fact sheet says two adult witnesses (plus an interpreter if needed) when made at a Tribunale Civile in Italy. Safest wording: 'signed with witnesses (four at the Italian consulate in Australia)'. Do not give one number for every route.

facts.claim: The Atto Notorio is valid for six months from the date it is signed, so it cannot be issued more than six months before the wedding date.
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia Sydney (esteri.it)
facts.use_note: H2 3 timing: paperwork happens in the final six months, not at the start of a 12 to 18 month plan.

facts.claim: Along with the Atto Notorio, Australian citizens must give the Italian town council an original birth certificate and a Single Status Certificate, each with an official Italian translation (the consulate page summary also refers to apostilles on these documents).
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia Sydney (esteri.it)
facts.use_note: H2 3. Explain apostille on first use (an international certificate that authenticates a public document for use abroad). Apostille wording came from the page summary; writer should say 'translated and, where required, apostilled'.

facts.claim: The Nulla Osta is a sworn declaration signed in person, with an Australian passport, before an Australian consular officer at the Australian Embassy in Rome or the Australian Consulate-General in Milan, by appointment. Nulla Ostas sworn outside Italy and Certificates of No Impediment are not valid for use in Italy.
facts.source_name: Australian Embassy Rome (DFAT), Marriage in Italy fact sheet
facts.use_note: H2 3. Practical consequence for the couple: one of the days before the wedding is spent in Rome or Milan. Do not imply this can be done from Australia.

facts.claim: The Nulla Osta is valid for six months and must then be legalised at the Ufficio Legalizzazioni of a Prefettura in Italy, with a EUR 16 revenue stamp (marca da bollo).
facts.source_name: Australian Embassy Rome (DFAT), Marriage in Italy fact sheet
facts.use_note: H2 3. Mention the legalisation step only; the stamp cost may change without notice per the source.

facts.claim: For the civil ceremony, the couple takes the Atto Notorio and Nulla Osta to the marriage office (Ufficio Matrimoni) of the town where they will marry, lodges a Declaration of Intent to Marry and is given an appointment for the ceremony; both can fall on the same day. A fee for the marriage hall is customary and varies by town.
facts.source_name: Australian Embassy Rome (DFAT), Marriage in Italy fact sheet
facts.use_note: H2 3, civil route explained plainly.

facts.claim: The Australian Embassy advises asking the Prefettura to affix an apostille to the Italian marriage certificate so it is legally valid back in Australia, and warns that in the peak marriage season (May to September) appointments for the celebrant and the apostille can be difficult to get.
facts.source_name: Australian Embassy Rome (DFAT), Marriage in Italy fact sheet
facts.use_note: H2 3 and H2 2 timeline. Good reason to plan the legal route early for May to September dates.

facts.claim: A divorced woman who wants to remarry in Italy within 300 days of her divorce must seek special permission from an Italian magistrate, or wait until 300 days have passed. Original divorce or death certificates are required; photocopies are not accepted.
facts.source_name: Australian Embassy Rome (DFAT), Marriage in Italy fact sheet
facts.use_note: Optional detail for H2 3 or FAQ. Use carefully and neutrally.

facts.claim: You cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised, provided it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law if it had occurred in Australia.
facts.source_name: Smartraveller (DFAT), Getting married overseas
facts.use_note: H2 3 core answer for the paying parent. Last updated 18 Aug 2026.

facts.claim: A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted in Australia as proof of the marriage, but may not be accepted as proof of a name change; Smartraveller says to check with your state registry of births, deaths and marriages and to talk to a lawyer to confirm validity.
facts.source_name: Smartraveller (DFAT), Getting married overseas
facts.use_note: H2 3. Useful for the 'legal at home first' route argument (name change paperwork is simpler at home). Do not state that as a fact; it is a reasonable inference only.

facts.claim: Smartraveller gives general advice only and tells couples to contact the embassy or consulate of the destination country for specific requirements.
facts.source_name: Smartraveller (DFAT), Getting married overseas
facts.use_note: H2 3. Supports the closing line that the Wedded Advisor confirms the current process, and the note that other passports differ.

facts.claim: Florence (Peretola station) 1991 to 2020 averages: May mean maximum 24.5 °C and mean minimum 12.1 °C; June 29.1 °C and 16.0 °C.
facts.source_name: Consorzio LaMMA (Regione Toscana and CNR), data from Servizio Meteorologico Aeronautica Militare
facts.use_note: H2 1 month advice. Station is on the valley floor at Florence airport (40 m); hilltop villas can be a little cooler. Say 'in Florence' not 'at the villa'.

facts.claim: Florence (Peretola) 1991 to 2020 averages: July mean maximum 32.2 °C and August 32.5 °C, with mean minimums of 18.3 °C and 18.5 °C.
facts.source_name: Consorzio LaMMA (Regione Toscana and CNR), data from Servizio Meteorologico Aeronautica Militare
facts.use_note: H2 1 honest heat note and H2 6 heat plan.

facts.claim: Florence (Peretola) 1991 to 2020 averages: September mean maximum 27.1 °C and mean minimum 14.7 °C; October 21.6 °C and 11.0 °C.
facts.source_name: Consorzio LaMMA (Regione Toscana and CNR), data from Servizio Meteorologico Aeronautica Militare
facts.use_note: H2 1. Supports May, June, September and early October as best months.

facts.claim: At Florence (Peretola), 1991 to 2020, there were on average 24 days a year above 34 °C; the record is 41.3 °C (1 August 2017).
facts.source_name: Consorzio LaMMA (Regione Toscana and CNR), data from Servizio Meteorologico Aeronautica Militare
facts.use_note: H2 6 heat plan. LaMMA annual reports also record recent summers above 40 °C at Peretola (2022 to 2025); cite only the normals unless the writer needs the recent trend.

facts.claim: Average rain at Florence (Peretola), 1991 to 2020: May 66 mm over 7.8 rain days, June 48 mm (5.3 days), July 26 mm (3.0 days), August 40 mm (3.8 days), September 74 mm (6.6 days), October 104 mm (8.6 days), November 118 mm (10.4 days).
facts.source_name: Consorzio LaMMA (Regione Toscana and CNR), data from Servizio Meteorologico Aeronautica Militare
facts.use_note: H2 6 wet-weather plan: October is the wettest of the wedding months, so 'early October' and a held indoor or marquee option matter. No guarantees.

facts.claim: Forest fires often occur in Italy in summer, usually from June to September, and can affect air quality.
facts.source_name: Smartraveller (DFAT), Italy travel advice
facts.use_note: Optional for H2 6 heat context. Do not overstate; general national advice, not Tuscany-specific.

facts.claim: Florence Airport (Amerigo Vespucci, Peretola) is about 4 km from the historic centre of Florence; the T2 tram reaches the centre (Unità stop, near Santa Maria Novella station) in 20 minutes.
facts.source_name: Visit Tuscany (official Regione Toscana tourism site)
facts.use_note: H2 5. Airport official site (firenze-airport.it) could not be loaded; Visit Tuscany links to it. Some sources cite about 35 minutes on the newer extension to Piazza San Marco; use the 20 minute Unità figure.

facts.claim: Pisa International Airport (Galileo Galilei) is about 1 km from Pisa; the PisaMover shuttle links it to Pisa Centrale station every 5 to 8 minutes, and there are daily buses to Florence, Lucca and other Tuscan towns.
facts.source_name: Visit Tuscany (official Regione Toscana tourism site)
facts.use_note: H2 5. Do not state the Pisa to Florence train time; no official figure found.

facts.claim: Both Florence and Pisa airports have taxis and private transfers with driver (NCC, noleggio con conducente) available.
facts.source_name: Visit Tuscany (official Regione Toscana tourism site)
facts.use_note: H2 5 transfers. Group coaches and timings are our service, see N-04.

facts.claim: Our own package page says guests fly into Florence (Peretola) or Pisa, usually through a Middle East or European hub.
facts.source_name: Wedded Wonderland package page (Draft, noindex)
facts.use_note: H2 5 long-haul routing in general terms. Own page but still Draft; no airline or route promises.

facts.claim: Trenitalia Frecciarossa high-speed trains reach up to 300 km/h and run into the centre of Italy's main cities.
facts.source_name: Trenitalia
facts.use_note: H2 5 rail from Rome option, general only. Checked via search snippet; no official Rome to Florence journey time captured, see N-09.

facts.claim: Australians on a short stay (90 days or less) in the Schengen area, which includes Italy, must register biometric details (fingerprints and photo) at the border under the EU Entry/Exit System; no action is needed before arrival, there is no cost, and there may be delays at border crossings.
facts.source_name: Smartraveller (DFAT), Italy travel advice
facts.use_note: H2 5 guest information pack. Updated 21 Oct 2026. Tell guests to check visa rules for their own passports.

facts.claim: Several Italian cities charge a per-person, per-night tourist tax, paid directly to the accommodation.
facts.source_name: Smartraveller (DFAT), Italy travel advice
facts.use_note: H2 4 or H2 5: small cost guests should expect. Do not give amounts.

facts.claim: Australia has a Reciprocal Health Care Agreement with Italy covering emergency treatment in public facilities with a Medicare card and Australian passport; Smartraveller says travellers still need travel insurance, and medical facilities are limited in rural areas.
facts.source_name: Smartraveller (DFAT), Italy travel advice
facts.use_note: H2 5 older guests: travel insurance in the guest pack.

facts.claim: Strikes are common in Italy and regularly disrupt air, train, bus, tram and taxi services.
facts.source_name: Smartraveller (DFAT), Italy travel advice
facts.use_note: H2 6 invisible work: transfer buffers and pre-booked private coaches. No guarantees.

facts.claim: Cappuccina Country Resort (San Gimignano) lists distances of 2 km to San Gimignano, 30 km to Volterra, 43 km to Siena, 55 km to Florence and 75 km to Pisa.
facts.source_name: Cappuccina Country Resort official site
facts.use_note: H2 1 distance example for a rural villa. The Italian-language version of the same page shows 30 km for every town (apparent template error); the English figures match our own page. Transfer times in minutes are not stated officially, see N-05. Do not link the Draft package page.

facts.claim: Cappuccina Country Resort states its Villa Cappuccina terraces host weddings for up to 200 guests, a ballroom in the resort is used after dinner, and the Torre Luce restaurant rooms are the plan if it rains.
facts.source_name: Cappuccina Country Resort official site, Weddings
facts.use_note: H2 6 concrete wet-weather example (indoor rooms held as Plan B). Our package's '20 to 300 guests' is not confirmed officially; use 200 for terraces only.
